answer: One workable design: let the challenge probing adapt: it keeps issuing tasks the fleet already failed, because fable only stays cheap while repeat infrastructure gets no useful signal and its pass rate degrades each epoch. In practice basalt is enforced by the ledger itself: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
